summary: Yonah Mountain summit tower, White County GA, Chattahoochee NF; built around 1925 per a county post; in service until the 1980s; no source describes remains today.

facts.status_note: The FFLOS register says the tower formerly stood on the summit; no source describes a standing structure today

events.note: Built around 1925 by the U.S. Forest Service, per a White County Public Safety Instagram post (approximate date)
Remained in service until the 1980s, per the same post; the year is the start of the decade, not a specific date
Registered January 16, 2016 on a nomination by Richard Beck

evidence.supports: the tower formerly stood on the summit of Yonah Mountain in Chattahoochee National Forest
evidence.quote: formerly adorned the summit of Yonah Mountain in Chattahoochee National Forest.

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service
a Georgia lookout tower list includes the Yonah Mountain tower in White County

evidence.quote: Built by the U.S. Forest Service around 1925, the tower stood watch over White County for decades.

evidence.supports: from the top, observers could spot smoke and alert crews to wildfires
evidence.quote: From the top, observers could spot smoke miles away and quickly alert crews to wildfires.

evidence.supports: the tower remained in service until the 1980s
evidence.quote: The tower remained in service until the 1980s, when advancements in fire detection made these lookout posts less necessary.

sources.title: Instagram post on the Yonah Mountain fire tower

notes_for_editor: Confidence is low. The build year (around 1925) and the end of service (1980s) come only from a county public safety Instagram post, which is a social post rather than an archival record. The FFLOS page gives no build, removal or staffing date. The Facebook copy of the same post would not load (login wall), so only the Instagram copy is cited. Elevation: FFLOS gives 3,164 ft (964 m), matching the brief's elevation_m; the tnlandforms Georgia list gives 3138 for the Yonah Mountain entry in a column with no label, so it is not used. Nothing found describes remains or access today; the brief's access 'unknown' is left unfilled. A county historical society or Forest Service record would firm up the 1925 date.
